CERTIFICATION OF TRUST — INFORMATION SHEET AND FORM
Prepared for The Jordan Lee Living Trust · March 14, 2020

DECLARATION — CERTIFICATION OF TRUST
This Certification of Trust is presented by Jordan Lee, as currently acting trustee of The Jordan Lee Living Trust, dated March 14, 2020, to First National Title Company in lieu of providing a copy of the complete trust instrument. It is offered under California Probate Code Section 18100.5 to establish the existence of the trust and Jordan Lee's authority to act as trustee, without disclosing the trust's dispositive provisions or other terms not called for by this certification.

WHAT A CERTIFICATION OF TRUST IS — PRESENTED IN LIEU OF THE TRUST INSTRUMENT
California law gives a trustee a specific alternative to handing over the complete trust instrument when a third party — such as a bank, title company, or escrow — needs to confirm a trust exists and that the trustee has authority to act for it: the trustee may present a certification of trust to any person in lieu of providing a copy of the trust instrument. A certification of trust can be executed on the trustee's own initiative or because the person the trustee is dealing with asked for one, and its function is to establish the existence or terms of the trust without disclosing the trust instrument itself.

A certification of trust may be executed by the trustee voluntarily or at the request of the person with whom the trustee is dealing."
  — Cal. Prob. Code § 18100.5(a) (California Legislative Information text), a certification of trust may be presented in lieu of the trust instrument (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PROB&sectionNum=18100.5.)

It states only that a certification of trust may be presented in lieu of the trust instrument and how it comes to be executed; it does not itself describe what the certification may or must contain (covered in a separate clause), any protection for a person relying on it, any right to demand excerpts, or any liability provision — those are separate subdivisions of this same section, addressed in other clauses in this document. No case law or secondary authority was consulted; this is the statutory text only.

WHAT A CERTIFICATION OF TRUST MAY CONTAIN AND WHAT IT MUST STATE
The statute lists what a certification of trust may confirm or contain: the existence of the trust and date of execution of the trust instrument; the identity of the settlor or settlors and the currently acting trustee or trustees; the powers of the trustee; the revocability or irrevocability of the trust and the identity of any person holding a power to revoke it; where there are multiple trustees, the signature authority of the trustees — that is, whether all or fewer than all currently acting trustees must sign to exercise various powers; the trust's identification number, whether a Social Security number or an employer identification number; the manner in which title to trust assets should be taken; and the legal description of any interest in real property held in the trust. Beyond that list of optional contents, the statute imposes two things the certification must state: that the trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in a way that would make the certification's representations incorrect, and that it is being signed by all of the currently acting trustees. The certification must be in the form of an acknowledged declaration signed by all currently acting trustees, and a certification signed by the currently acting trustee may be recorded with the county recorder in the county where all or part of any described real property is located.

CERTIFICATION OF TRUST — FILLABLE CONTENT
CERTIFICATION OF TRUST

1. Existence of trust and date of execution. The Jordan Lee Living Trust is a trust, and the trust instrument establishing it was executed on March 14, 2020.

2. Settlor(s). The settlor(s) of the trust is/are: Jordan Lee.

3. Currently acting trustee(s). The currently acting trustee(s) of the trust is/are: Jordan Lee. Any successor trustee named to act upon a vacancy is: Pat Morgan.

4. Powers of the trustee. The trustee's powers under the trust instrument include: Full power to buy, sell, and manage trust property; any one trustee may act alone.

5. Revocability. The trust is revocable by the settlor, Jordan Lee.

6. Signature authority of multiple trustees. Where more than one person is a currently acting trustee, the signature(s) required to exercise the powers of the trustee are as follows: Full power to buy, sell, and manage trust property; any one trustee may act alone.

7. Trust taxpayer identification number. The trust's identification number (Social Security number or employer identification number) is: XX-XXXXXXX.

8. Manner of taking title. Title to trust assets acquired in connection with this certification should be taken as follows: Jordan Lee, Trustee of the Jordan Lee Living Trust dated March 14, 2020.

The undersigned trustee(s) certify that the trust described above has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner that would cause the representations made in this certification to be incorrect, and that this certification is signed by all of the currently acting trustees of the trust. This certification does not include, and is not required to include, the dispositive provisions of The Jordan Lee Living Trust or the manner in which the trust estate is to be distributed.

EXCERPTS ARE OPTIONAL FOR THE TRUSTEE TO INCLUDE, BUT A THIRD PARTY MAY REQUIRE THEM
The statute gives the trustee discretion, not an obligation, to attach source material: a certification of trust may, but is not required to, include excerpts from the original trust documents, any amendments, and any other documents evidencing or pertaining to the succession of successor trustees, and the certification is not required to contain the trust's dispositive provisions — the terms setting out how the trust estate is distributed. That trustee-side discretion is paired with a third-party-side right: a person whose interest is or may be affected by the certification may require the trustee offering or recording it to provide copies of excerpts from the original trust documents, any amendments, and any other documents that designate, evidence, or pertain to the succession of the trustee, or that confer on the trustee the power to act in the pending transaction, or both. The statute is explicit that neither the trustee's discretion nor the third party's right to require excerpts is intended to require or imply an obligation to disclose the trust's dispositive provisions or the entire trust and its amendments.

PROTECTION FOR A THIRD PARTY WHO RELIES ON A CERTIFICATION IN GOOD FAITH
The statute protects a person who relies on a certification of trust without knowing better: a person who acts in reliance upon a certification of trust without actual knowledge that the representations contained in it are incorrect is not liable to any person for so acting, and a person without actual knowledge that the certification's facts are incorrect may assume without inquiry that those facts exist — actual knowledge is not inferred merely because the relying person happens to hold a copy of all or part of the trust instrument. That protection extends to the transaction itself: any transaction, and any lien it creates, entered into by the trustee and a person relying on a certification of trust is enforceable against the trust assets, except that if the person has actual knowledge the trustee is acting outside the scope of the trust, the transaction is not enforceable against the trust assets. The statute also preserves a separate channel of accountability: nothing in this reliance protection limits the rights of the trust's beneficiaries against the trustee.

LIABILITY FOR REFUSING A CERTIFICATION AND DEMANDING THE COMPLETE TRUST DOCUMENTS IN BAD FAITH
The statute pairs a non-inference rule with a liability provision aimed at refusals to accept a certification. Subdivision (h)'s liability provision does not apply when a beneficiary makes the demand, when the demand arises in litigation concerning the trust, or to the extent a person is exercising the excerpt right described in subdivision (e). This document does not separately cover subdivision (i), which addresses recording a certification of trust with the county recorder for real property purposes and the recorder's fee — that subdivision was fetched and verified along with the rest of the section but is not the subject of any clause in this document because it falls outside the topics requested. No case law or secondary authority was consulted; this is the statutory text only.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned, being all of the currently acting trustees of The Jordan Lee Living Trust, have signed this Certification of Trust on the date written below.

_________________________ Date: September 4, 2026
Jordan Lee, Trustee

This certification is executed in the form of an acknowledged declaration, to be signed before a notary public or other officer authorized to take acknowledgments. A notary public or other officer completing a notarial certificate for this certification verifies only the identity of the individual who signed the document, not the truthfulness, accuracy, or validity of its contents.
